title: Graceful failure: orchestrated probe strategy for stable autoscaling and multi-region failover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current readiness/liveness probes are binary and noisy during transient load spikes and KV-cache warmup. This causes flapping autoscaler decisions and unnecessary multi-region failovers, increasing tail latency and cost. Goal: design and implement an orchestrated probe strategy that smooths health signals, enables graceful degradation, and stabilizes autoscaling decisions while preserving SLOs across regions.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy a probe orchestration layer that outputs three signals: stable_ok, degraded_ok, and critical_fail
Autoscaler uses stable_ok/degraded_ok windows to make scale decisions and never scales down below a configured reserve during degraded_ok
Multi-region failover uses critical_fail only after quorum of regional critical_fail signals or after sustained degraded_ok across primaries for >N seconds
Production experiment shows 30% reduction in autoscaler-induced scaling churn during traffic spikes and no regression in 99th percentile latency SLOs (target: <= 450ms) over 72h
Runbook updated with new probe semantics, troubleshooting checklist, and rollback steps
proposed_solution: Introduce a small sidecar (probe-orchestrator) that consumes existing k8s readiness/liveness checks and internal runtime metrics (queue depth, kv-cache hit rate, avg token latency) and publishes three semantic health endpoints. Implement exponential smoothing + stateful windows to reduce sensitivity to single-sample noise. Wire the autoscaler to use proportional logic: scale-up quickly on stable_ok loss, scale-down conservatively while degraded_ok persists. For multi-region, create a regional aggregator that applies hysteresis and only triggers failover when critical_fail is observed by >50% of healthy AZs or when degraded_ok persists beyond N minutes and capacity headroom is below threshold.
tradeoffs: Adding a sidecar increases pod resource footprint and deployment complexity but centralizes logic and avoids changing existing runtime probes
Longer smoothing windows reduce false positives but increase failover reaction time for real outages
Conservative scale-down reduces cost savings but improves stability and SLO adherence
Regional quorum logic may delay failover for partial-region catastrophic failures; mitigated by AZ-aware critical_fail aggregation
implementation_steps: Prototype probe-orchestrator as a lightweight Go service consuming /metrics and internal probe endpoints
Define canonical health signal schema and implement three endpoints: /health/stable, /health/degraded, /health/critical
Add configurable smoothing parameters (alpha, window_seconds) and reserve_capacity knob for autoscaler
Patch HPA/CustomAutoscaler to read new endpoints and map signals to scaling policies
Build regional aggregator service (stateless with short retention) to compute region-level health
Run shadow autoscaling for 2 weeks against a subset of services and collect telemetry
Rollout canary to non-critical customer-facing endpoints, monitor SLOs and cost metrics, then expand
tests: Unit tests for smoothing logic and state transitions (stable->degraded->critical)
Integration tests with autoscaler in k8s test cluster simulating step traffic increases and KV-cache cold-starts
Chaos tests: inject partial pod CPU starvation and network latency to validate hysteresis and multi-region quorum
End-to-end experiment: 72h A/B comparison between control and orchestrated-probe on 10% of production traffic
open_questions: What default smoothing window balances cache-warmup transient spikes vs. real degradation? Suggest initial 30s with alpha=0.2 for experiments
Should the orchestrator be a sidecar per pod or a shared daemon per node? Sidecar gives pod-local signals but higher overhead; daemon reduces footprint but may mask pod-level failures
How to expose these signals to managed dedicated and private deployments where k8s hooks differ? Need platform adapters
Operationally, what SLO thresholds should map to degraded_ok vs critical_fail for different customer tiers?
decisions: Prototype as a sidecar per pod for maximum signal fidelity (decision made 2026-03-04)
Use three-tier semantic health outputs to decouple autoscaling logic from strict liveness/readiness checks (decision made 2026-03-05)
Autoscaler will adopt conservative scale-down with a minimum reserved replica count configurable per service (decision made 2026-03-08)
Multi-region failover requires quorum of AZ-level critical_fail or sustained degraded_ok + low headroom (decision made 2026-03-10)
Expose configuration via runtime-1.22 feature flags and Console rollout toggles (decision made 2026-03-11)
notes: Related: ENG-4921 and ENG-11234 had earlier probe-windowing ideas but were focused on signal filtering; this ticket centralizes orchestration and multi-region logic
Leverage existing KV-cache hit metrics exported by runtime (metric names: runtime_kv_hit_rate and runtime_queue_depth)
Benchmark results (shadow run): preliminary shows 28% reduction in scale-down churn; full A/B pending
